newsitem.title: USA: Tele-Comms expects positive free cash flow.
newsitem.headline: Tele-Comms expects positive free cash flow.

text.p: Tele-Communications Inc's free cash flow will move into the plus area in 1997 for the first time in several years, a company spokeswoman said on Monday.
Capital spending in 1997 is expected to decline from the $1.6 billion to $2 billion forecast to be spent this year, she said, athough next year's figures were not available.

She defined free cash flow as EBITDA minus income expense and minus capital expenditures, adding that TCI will be moving from the costly development phase into the implementation phase in some key areas of its businesses.
EBITDA stands for earnings before income, taxation, depreciation and amortization and is commonly referred to as an indicator of cash flow for companies with high debt.
